description: 7 piezo sensors, one hit event per struck note (no sustain/duration, no breath, no check-button convention -- the hit itself is the check, per docs project doc claude/controller_hid_protocol.md). Pad numbering/names below (1-7) are AUTHORITATIVE, matching the physical build's HID report layout exactly (button N = pad N, no offset, since drum-kit has no separate check bit): 1=Kick, 2=Snare, 3=Hi-Hat, 4=High Tom, 5=Floor Tom, 6=Crash, 7=Ride -- keep this file and docs/beatmap_schema.md's drum pad table in sync if either changes. The list order below is NOT the same as pad-number order -- it's sorted by approximate perceptual pitch (kick lowest ... ride highest), which is what the converter's piano-mode bass-clef bucketing walks across low-to-high; each entry still carries its correct authoritative 'index'/'name'. Band mode (a real drum/percussion MusicXML part) is NOT YET matching by percussion instrument name -- it currently falls back to the same pitch-bucketing as piano mode. That's a known gap, worth revisiting once there's an actual drum-kit MusicXML to test against (drum-kit hardware itself isn't built yet either). band_mode_name_map below is prepared for that future work but isn't consulted by convert.py yet.
